items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: they had another fellow who used to play a plunger, like the old Sam Nanton (PHONETIC) player with Ellington.

ctx.x: Had a great trombone player by the name of Fred Beckett (PHONETIC). He was one of the smoothest, cleanest trombonists that you'd ever hear in life. We used to call him Black Dorsey. He could -- a very sensuous type of player, just a gorgeous player. He died at an early age with tuberculosis. We had Ray Perry that played electric violin, who was probably one of the best jazz violinists that ever was. He died at an early age. Then Dexter Gordon was in the

band, tenor saxophone player, Illinois Jacquet. Jack MacVeigh was baritone saxophone player, and I. Then Ernie Royal, trumpet player, and Carl George was there for a while and Joe Newman and they had another fellow who used to play a plunger, like the old Sam Nanton (PHONETIC) player with Ellington. We called him "Mushmouth." It was Sonny Craven (PHONETIC).
